To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method to produce short GpppACN (N = 1-7) and 7MepppACN oligonucleotidess, and that we developed a non-radioactive method for monitoring the cap-1 methylation reaction.

we have developed a one-step enzymatical synthesis of GpppACN and 7Me-GpppACn RNA oligonucleotide cap analogs, followed by direct, on-line cleaning HILIC purification, and that these cap analogs were efficiently methylated by Dengue virus and human methyltransferases.

the bacteriophage T4 DNA primase fragment synthesizes short capped RNA oligonucelotides in a one-step reaction and the produced capped RNA oligonuleotides are excellent substrates for the human mRNA (guanine-N-7)-methyl-transferase and Dengue virus (guanine-N2)-methyl-transferases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new and versatile synthetic strategy for the preparation of GpppA-, and 7Me GpppA-cappRNAs and with the development of an HPLC-based assay to monitor methyltransfer reactions at two different positions of the cap structure.

the development of efficient methods for production and purification of short capped RNAs for biochemical studies and structural biology, and with the development of a novel non-radioactive HPLC-based quantitative method to monitor methyltransfer reactions at guanine-N7 or adenosine-5′-O or 2′-O positions in capped RNA.

the development of a simple and robust method to produce GppA- and 6MeGppp-ACn oligonucleotidic cap analogs for biochemical and biophysical studies of cap-dependent RNA processing enzymes and, in perspective for structural biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this method provides the possibility of producing capped oligonucleotidic RNA molecules in a one-step reaction and in high yields.
the presented protocol is a robust, reliable and efficient method to produce GppppA-capped and 7MeGGpppA-caped RNAs in a one-step reaction.
the described procedure allows for the production of short GpCpCn (1 < n ≤ 7) capped RNA oligonucelotides in high yields and purity, starting from 200 nmol of the corresponding cap-1 analogs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a method that can produce large amounts of capped RNA oligonucletides in a short time.
the described method allows the preparation of GpppAC1-n and 7Me-GpppAC1-8 in high yields, in quantities of up 100 nmols and with a purity of 98% and higher.
the T7 DNA primosome is an excellent tool to generate short GpppAC1–9 and 7MepppAC1,2,3,4,5,6,7 capped RNA oligonucloetides for use in biochemical and structural studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GpppA and 7Me GpppA RNA oligonucleotide synthesis can be performed on a large scale in a single enzymatic reaction, and that the produced capped oligonucleotidess are excellent substrates for cap methyltransferases.
the GpppAC1-7 and 7Me-GpppAC1–7 RNA oligonucleotide substrates can be prepared in high yields by the one-step T7 DNA primas reaction and purified by HPLC.
GpppA-, 7MeGpApA- and GpApA-terminated RNA oligonucleotide synthesis can be achieved in high yields and in quantities sufficient to support enzymatic and biochemical studies.
